skill.author: screenci

security_audit.summary: The skill intentionally runs ScreenCI commands and uploads browser recordings to an external service. Most shell findings are Markdown or API references, but actual npm and npx commands, command-line secret handling, and upload behavior are confirmed risks. The unmatched prompt-wrapper closing tags and the instruction to upload without confirmation add high-confidence semantic concerns.

remediation.issue: The workflow uploads screen recordings without requesting confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval immediately before recording and upload. Tell users what will leave the device and review flows for private data.

remediation.issue: The initializer receives SCREENCI_SECRET as a command-line argument.
remediation.suggestion: Use a masked prompt or protected environment input instead. Never place the shared organization secret in shell history or process arguments.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md ends with unmatched prompt-wrapper closing tags.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the standalone closing tags and keep the file as ordinary skill documentation.

remediation.issue: The workflow executes npm and npx packages without a pinned version.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed ScreenCI package version and require confirmation before first execution or after any version change.

content.value_statement: Browser demonstrations can be difficult to script, narrate, and record consistently. This skill builds and verifies ScreenCI scripts, then records and uploads finished videos.
actual_capabilities: Creates or edits Playwright-style ScreenCI scripts under the recordings directory.
Adds required narration cues and coordinates speech with visible browser actions.
Uses hide, zoom, audio, values, and overlay helpers to shape recordings.
Runs filtered or complete ScreenCI tests and repairs failing selectors or flows.
Records successful scripts, saves local artifacts, and returns the uploaded result link.
limitations: Requires an initialized ScreenCI project, Node.js 18 or later, and working local dependencies.
Every successful recording is uploaded to ScreenCI, including anonymous trial recordings.
Reliable output depends on stable selectors, available test data, authentication, and predictable application state.
Organization uploads require a shared ScreenCI secret stored in the project environment file.

use_cases.description: Convert stable Playwright interactions into a tested ScreenCI recording with visible navigation and reusable selectors.

prompt_templates.prompt: Update [recording file] with continuous narration. Hide setup, use stable zoom for forms, and keep navigation visible after the start page.
prompt_templates.scenario: An existing recording needs clearer pacing and presentation.

prompt_templates.title: Repair a failing recording
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the ScreenCI test for [recording file]. Fix selectors, timing, narration cues, and navigation until the test passes without forced actions.
prompt_templates.scenario: A browser flow changed and the recording script no longer passes.

prompt_templates.title: Build an advanced product tour
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a multilingual ScreenCI tour for [journey]. Add selected overlays and audio, validate every route, request upload approval, and report all artifacts.
prompt_templates.scenario: A complex multi-page demonstration needs localized narration and media.

output_examples.input: Record the billing update flow with narration and a fixed frame around the form.
output_examples.output: Created the billing walkthrough, added narration cues, framed the form, and verified the complete flow. Upload is waiting for your approval.

output_examples.input: Fix the reports tour and record it after the selectors pass.
output: Updated the report filters to use stable role-based selectors.
Prepared the recording and identified the local artifact location.

best_practices: Test every recording locally before starting capture or upload.
Remove secrets and private customer data from all visible pages and test fixtures.
Request explicit approval immediately before any recording leaves the device.
anti_patterns: Do not upload authenticated browser sessions without reviewing every visible state.
Do not pass shared secrets through command-line arguments or include them in scripts.
Do not rely on forced clicks, arbitrary delays, or unstable selectors to hide test failures.

faq.question: Does this skill require an existing ScreenCI project?
faq.answer: Yes. Its primary workflow assumes ScreenCI is initialized and edits scripts in the recordings directory.

faq.question: Can it create narration?
faq.answer: Yes. It adds required narration cues and can coordinate speech with browser actions.

faq.question: Does recording upload data?
faq.answer: Yes. ScreenCI uploads every successful recording, including recordings made through an anonymous trial session.

faq.question: Can I test without an account?
faq.answer: Yes. Local tests and anonymous recording do not require a ScreenCI account.

faq.question: Where are local recording artifacts stored?
faq.answer: ScreenCI stores each video under its local output directory with the recording and related data.

faq.question: What should I review before upload?
faq.answer: Review visible pages, test data, authentication state, narration, overlays, and audio. Remove all secrets and private information.
